answer:
I cleaned up all 10 English product files and wrote a Spanish version of each one. A final search of the product folder, Spanish files included, found no em dashes (—), en dashes (–) or arrows (→).

**English cleanup** (`product/00-outreach-scripts.md` through `product/09-welcome-emails.md`)
- The headings now use colons: "Outreach Scripts: First Paid Client", "Step 1: outreach scripts in practice".
- In the body text I replaced each dash or arrow with a comma, colon or full stop, whichever read best. For example, "Track every reply → it tells you…" is now "Track every reply. It tells you what to fix next."
- I only changed punctuation. The wording, the order of the tips and the six-step layout are the same.

**Spanish versions** (`product/es/`, same file names)
- Each file matches its English file: the same headings, six steps and tips in the same order. I used the informal "tú", which works across Latin America and Spain.
- Each English tip has one fixed Spanish wording, used the same way everywhere. For example, "Track every reply" is always "Registra cada respuesta", and "Set one follow-up date and keep it" is always "Fija una fecha de seguimiento y cúmplela".
- The titles are: Guiones de contacto, Plantilla de propuesta, Plan de 30 días, Hoja de cálculo de precios, Preguntas para la llamada de descubrimiento, Portafolio en un día, Plantilla de testimonio, Registro de clientes, Tarifario and Correos de bienvenida.

One choice to check: "Scope creep starts with silence" has no common Spanish phrase, so I wrote "El alcance se desborda cuando callas" (roughly, "the scope overflows when you stay quiet"). Tell me if you'd prefer different wording.

If you'd like a different variety of Spanish, such as Rioplatense "vos", I can switch all 10 Spanish files to it.
